name: PTSD Coach
summary: Official VA/DoD-developed app offering tools to track PTSD symptoms, learn coping skills, and access support anytime — free for everyone.
description: PTSD Coach is a free mobile app created by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs’ National Center for PTSD and the Department of Defense. It provides information about PTSD, self-screening tools, symptom tracking, and evidence-based coping tools (relaxation, grounding, positive self-talk, safety planning, support contacts) to help manage trauma-related stress. Available on iOS and Android (and online).
patient_summary: PTSD Coach helps you understand PTSD, track how you feel, and access coping tools and support resources wherever you are. It’s designed to help with trauma-related symptoms, flashbacks, anxiety, sleep problems and distress. It can be used on its own for support or alongside therapy — but it’s *not* a replacement for professional treatment if you’re in crisis.

primary_uses: Support planning and access to help resources

linked_conditions.context: PTSD Coach offers tools and self-assessment designed specifically for people who have experienced trauma, to help manage distress, flashbacks, nightmares, and hyperarousal.
Due to overlap between PTSD and depression symptoms, consistent use of coping tools and symptom tracking may help reduce depressive symptoms and support overall mental health.
Relaxation, grounding and self-management tools may help reduce anxiety and improve emotional regulation in individuals with trauma-related anxiety.

contraindications: Not a substitute for professional evaluation, psychotherapy, or medication.
Not appropriate as the only support for individuals with severe PTSD, active suicidal ideation, psychosis, or unstable conditions.
Self-assessment scores are not diagnostic — consider professional assessment for official diagnosis.
Use with caution: some tools may trigger strong emotions, especially for trauma survivors; having a support system is recommended.

efficacy_data.comparison_data: Among users with at least two assessments over 12 months
efficacy_data.patient_text: In real-world use, about one in three users who repeatedly used PTSD Coach and completed assessments reported meaningful reductions in PTSD symptoms over time.

conditions: Sleep problems, nightmares, hyperarousal linked to trauma
exclusions: Active suicidal ideation or self-harm risk without safety plan
Severe mental illness (psychosis) without close clinical supervision
Untreated severe substance use disorders (ideally stabilize before relying on self-help app alone)

data_collected: Usage data (which tools used, how often)
Optional user-added customizations (saved contacts, music, photos)
Device information and minimal app metadata
data_shared: None beyond aggregated internal analytics (per developer statements)
No selling of data to advertisers (per Play Store privacy listing)

sections.heading: What PTSD Coach Does
sections.text: PTSD Coach helps you learn about trauma and PTSD, track your symptoms over time, and access a toolbox of coping strategies — relaxation, grounding, breathing exercises, positive self-talk, safety planning, and support contact access — all in one app. It was developed by the VA and DoD to support trauma survivors, veterans, and anyone dealing with post-traumatic stress.

sections.heading: How Well Does It Work?
sections.comparison: Users with repeated assessments over 12 months
sections.text: In a large real-world cohort, ~32% of users who completed multiple PTSD assessments experienced clinically significant symptom reduction over time. In a small pilot RCT, users reported reduced distress and found the app acceptable and useful for managing symptoms. While promising, results are modest and app should be used as part of a broader treatment plan when needed.
sections.patient_text: Some people notice their trauma-related symptoms (flashbacks, sleep, anxiety) get milder with consistent use. PTSD Coach is especially useful when combined with support, therapy, or other care.

citation.title: User engagement with and outcomes from PTSD Coach: a 12-month real-world study

sections.heading: Who Should Use PTSD Coach?
sections.text: PTSD Coach is best for people who:
items: Have experienced trauma and are experiencing PTSD symptoms or trauma-related distress
Want a free, easily accessible app to manage symptoms when they arise
Prefer self-guided coping tools and accessible resources (anytime, no appointment needed)
Need to track symptoms, triggers, and progress over time
Are already in or considering therapy — app works as a supplement, not a replacement
not_recommended: People with active suicidal ideation, severe PTSD, psychosis, or severe comorbidities who need intensive, supervised care
Those looking for passive relaxation apps — PTSD Coach is likely to prompt reflection, self-assessment, and active coping
Anyone using the app as the only form of mental health care without a safety plan or support network

items.description: Use built-in validated checklists to assess PTSD symptoms and track your scores over time. Helps you monitor changes and notice patterns.
items.evidence: Demonstrated utility in naturalistic study — repeated assessments associated with symptom reductions in a subset of users. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search4{CITATION_END}

items.feature: Coping tools: relaxation, breathing, grounding, mindfulness, positive self-talk
items.description: Access coping exercises like guided breathing, calming sounds/images, grounding strategies, mood-management tools, and self-talk prompts when triggered or feeling distressed.
items.evidence: PTSD Coach was designed using evidence-based self-help techniques recommended by mental health professionals and reviewed by VA/DoD. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search25{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search7{CITATION_END}

items.description: Save trusted contacts, photos, music, or personalized coping items. Easily access crisis hotlines, mental-health resources, and external support from within the app.
items.evidence: Having quick access to safety planning and support contacts increases user safety and ability to manage crises outside of therapy sessions. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search2{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search9{CITATION_END}

items.description: Learn about what PTSD is, how common symptoms are, what treatments and coping strategies work — useful if you’re newly recognizing trauma effects or supporting someone else.
items.evidence: PTSD Coach includes vetted psychoeducation materials from VA National Center for PTSD. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search2{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search26{CITATION_END}

items.feature: Symptom tracking over time & progress visualization
items.description: Track your PCL-5 scores, triggers, moods, sleep, and other factors over time — useful for noticing patterns, progress, or triggers and sharing with a clinician if desired.
items.evidence: Regular self-monitoring is a recognized component of self-management and can support greater self-awareness and engagement in recovery. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search9{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search4{CITATION_END}

sections.heading: Cost & Access
sections.text: PTSD Coach is completely free to download and use (no subscription or paywall). All tools, assessments, and features are accessible at no cost.

sections.heading: Privacy & Data Security
sections.summary: PTSD Coach does not require login, stores data locally on device, and does not share data with third parties beyond aggregated analytics. However, it is *not* a HIPAA-governed system — treat data as you would with any wellness app and secure your device accordingly.
items: No user login required — data stored locally or optionally exported by user
No forced data sharing or sale of personal data (developer states no data sale) {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search1{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search26{CITATION_END}
Encryption in transit for any network communications (e.g., support links)
Optional export of custom safety plans or self-reports to share with clinicians (user-initiated)
User responsible for device-level security (PIN, biometrics) if storing sensitive mood or trauma data
data_collected: Self-report symptom assessments (PCL-5 or in-app symptom checklists)
Tool usage data (which coping tools you used, when)
Optional custom user content (contacts, photos, music) — stored on device
Device/app metadata for analytics (with user consent) — anonymized
data_shared: Aggregated, anonymized usage analytics (per VA/DoD statements) for public-health evaluation purposes {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search2{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search4{CITATION_END}

sections.heading: What PTSD Coach Does
sections.text: PTSD Coach helps you understand trauma and PTSD, offers symptom self-assessment and tracking, and gives you a toolbox of coping strategies — all in your pocket. You get grounding exercises, relaxation tools, safety planning, support contact access, psychoeducation, and the option to track your symptoms over time.

sections.heading: How Well Does It Work?
sections.comparison: Users with repeated assessments over 12 months
sections.text: In a real-world naturalistic study of users who completed multiple assessments, about one-third experienced a clinically significant symptom improvement over time. A pilot RCT found the app acceptable and helpful. While not a substitute for therapy, PTSD Coach shows promise as a self-management companion for people affected by trauma. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search4{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search14{CITATION_END}
sections.patient_text: Many people find that using PTSD Coach regularly — especially when they’re in a safe space — helps them cope with triggers, manage stress, and reduce PTSD symptoms. Results vary; the app is best used as a complement to therapy or other care.

sections.heading: Who Should Use PTSD Coach?
sections.text: PTSD Coach is best for people who:
items: Have experienced trauma and have PTSD or trauma-related symptoms
Want on-the-go coping tools (grounding, breathing, relaxation) available at any time
Prefer self-guided support or need something between therapy sessions
Are willing to track symptoms and engage actively with the app
Need a free, no-cost, no-login option for trauma self-help
not_recommended: Those in crisis (suicidal thoughts, active self-harm, psychosis) — they need professional help immediately
People expecting the app alone to treat severe PTSD — it works best as part of a broader care plan
Users who dislike self-assessment or frequent reminders of trauma — some may find symptom tracking triggering
Those needing HIPAA-grade data security or full medical-record compliance

faqs.a: Yes. PTSD Coach is 100% free and contains no ads or in-app purchases. It's provided by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs and DoD as a public mental-health resource. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search2{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search21{CITATION_END}

faqs.q: Is PTSD Coach a replacement for therapy?
faqs.a: No. PTSD Coach is meant as a self-help tool and companion — it does not replace professional evaluation, psychotherapy, or medication when needed. It works best as part of a broader recovery or care plan. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search28{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search8{CITATION_END}

faqs.q: Can PTSD Coach help immediately if I’m triggered?
faqs.a: Yes — PTSD Coach includes coping tools such as grounding, relaxation, breathing, and positive self-talk that can be used on-the-spot when you feel triggered, anxious, or overwhelmed. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search26{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search7{CITATION_END}

faqs.q: Does the app require login or payment?
faqs.a: No. You can use PTSD Coach without creating an account, and all features are free. {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search21{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search2{CITATION_END}

faqs.q: Is my data private and secure?
faqs.a: Data entered into the app is stored locally on your device; VA/DoD do not sell or share personal data. However — because it’s not a HIPAA-governed system — treat sensitive entries like you would any wellness app (use device lock, avoid sharing sensitive logs). {CITATION_START}cite{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search2{CITATION_DELIMITER}turn0search26{CITATION_END}
